thread:
sam: Heads-up — we've been seeing steady SLO drift in us-west-2 for the last ~20m, p50 ~30ms -> 60ms, p95 spikes to 1.1s. Queue depth on inference workers is climbing.
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: region(us-west-2) inference_queue_depth > 80% for 15m — PagerDuty triggered
elaine: copy. I'm seeing continuous small requests (mostly short chat turns) that are keeping the packing window open. Not classic cold-start — this looks like queue piling from many tiny seq requests.
leon: prometheus snippet I ran:
```
sum(rate(runtime_inference_queue_length{region="us-west-2"}[5m])) by (shard)
```
nodes 3 and 7 show sustained >120 qps queued. Also net egress on those nodes is unusually high.
kevin: any network flakiness hints? if connections are stalling, batching will hold until timeout and then flush, causing longer tail.
maya: checked infra logs — some tcp retransmits around 2005001060 for the us-west-2 vpc gateway. infra-bot forwarded the flow logs.
infra-bot: Attached flow log excerpt:
```
[2005001058] src=10.10.7.12 dst=10.10.8.9 flags=PA retransmits=3 rtt_ms=120
[2005001062] src=10.10.3.4 dst=10.10.7.12 flags=PA retransmits=1 rtt_ms=95
```
sam: good catch. If KV cache prefill or small-message packing gets delayed by network stalls, admission will keep accepting requests into the batch window and delay dispatch.
elaine: mitigation suggestions:
- temporarily cap per-shard inflight admission to lower headroom (reduce packing backlog)
- apply short-term throttles on best-effort customers (tier=free)
- route a subset of traffic to smaller quantized model variant (faster per-token but slightly lower quality)
kevin: operational steps I'd run:
1) `curl -XPOST https://infra-api/regions/us-west-2/shards/scale -d '{"delta":2}'` to add 2 hot shards
2) bump admission throttler config: `admission.max_inflight_per_shard=70`
3) enable route fallback: `routing.policy=region:us-west-2->model:small-q4f` for 5% traffic
leon: I can roll step 2 now. rolling update will take ~30s per shard.
maya: I can open a firewall ticket with VPC team to trace the gateway. But that's medium term.
oncall-bot: Action logged: kevin requested shard add and admission cap change. Runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/inference/queue-pileup
sam: let's do the quick config change first (admission cap) + route 5% to small-q4f. kevin please coordinate shard add if we still see backlog after 5m.
kevin: rolling admission change now: `PATCH /config/admission` -> `{"max_inflight_per_shard":70}`
infra-bot: Config change applied to shards [3,7,9]. New value confirmed.
leon: immediate effect: queue depth per those shards dropping ~40% in 90s, p95 tail reduced to ~420ms (was 1.1s). p50 back to ~32ms.
sam: nice, keep monitoring. Maya, please keep the VPC tracing active. We'll hold off shard add for now.
maya: got it. I've added packet-capture for the gateway between 2005001120-2005001220 and pinged networking team. Ticket #NET-834.
elaine: follow-up items:
- adjust admission smoothing to avoid re-opening packing window on transient network jitter
- add a routing fallback test in canary to flip 5% to small-q4f automatically when queue depth > 60%
- cost check on running extra shards if we need to scale for longer
kevin: noted. I'll draft a PR to the admission controller to add a jitter-tolerant flush threshold.
sam: thanks all. marking this thread as 'monitoring' — will update in 10m with metrics. :eyes:
oncall-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Close candidate in 2h if stable.
